reviews.title: worst ever app
reviews.text:
Alight Motion for me is often criticized for its performance issues and limitations, which makes many users feel it’s one of the weakest editing apps compared to more advanced options. The app can lag heavily on mid-range or older devices, causing slow previews, choppy timelines, and frequent crashes. Its rendering times are notoriously long, especially when using effects, motion blur, or high-resolution settings. Many creators also complain that the app struggles with smooth playback, making it hard to time transitions or effects accurately. These problems make editing feel frustrating and inconsistent.

Another major issue is the app’s limited professional features and paywall structure. Many essential tools—such as certain effects, fonts, and export settings—are locked behind a subscription, which can feel restrictive for beginners or casual users. Even with the paid version, Alight Motion still lacks the advanced stabilization, 3D tools, and color-grading controls offered by other mobile editing apps. Combined with watermarks for unpaid users and interface glitches, Alight Motion often feels outdated and unreliable, causing many editors to switch to alternatives like CapCut or After Effects for more stability and creative freedom.
